heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings (two uniform 256-bit words each); their chaining values CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: for every fixed variant a0, Pr[W7x in F7] = p7 = 287,309,824/2^32 exactly, and given it (W0..W6) is uniform and independent of W7 (Lemma 5.1); E16x is uniform for a good pair, so a lane passes the 8 tested bits with probability 2^-8 and the row-16 set with probability 160/2^32; the expected numbers of passing classes (0.53516) and good pairs (13,152) per first block; independence across first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected counts per first block that fix the work (V_MAX), the law of the second-block words that defines q3, and the independence of the first blocks (proof.md Sections 5 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact distribution of the number of passing classes over all 2^32 values of A_{-1} for the 8 classes (p8hits.c, Appendix A.2); 29,360,128 (2^22 + 2^23 + 2^24) real first blocks through the attack's own filters with the 8 classes (proof.md Section 13.1, e2ep8.c): passing classes, good pairs and stage-3a passes within 0.07% of their expectations, 14,199 row-16 passes against 14,385.0 expected (z = -1.55), every one checked exactly in Python (the first block gives the chaining value, the variant is selected, rows -4..16 hold in both members); the organizer experiment a0-online-r38.
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem; tested on 2^24 first blocks, not 2^82. The class tests of one first block are correlated (at most 2 of the 8 classes pass); only the expectations and the exact probability that some class passes enter the ledger.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 196,608 selected variants (the 8 classes of mask 7fe96c7c) of Pr[the pair is in the accepted event: rows 16..21 of both members follow every cell, '+' pair and two-bit condition of P8 closing at rows 16..21, row 19 on its signed differences only, the relation E18 = E17 (bits 24, 23, 15) not imposed, and the state words A34..A37, E34..E37 of the two members are equal]; q3 >= q3_model = 2^-96.0133.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Our preregistered measurements: (1) the printed-cell event (proof.md Section 7.4 and Appendix A.12; preregistration hashed before the first seed): traillab, 128 fresh seeds x 2^28 window samples on real compressions with the real message expansion, row 16 exact (the 160-word set), W8 drawn from the 196,608 selected variants, W6 uniform, W7 uniform in F7, the accepted event counted (prefix rows 16..21 times zero output difference): mean 2^-96.3123, seed sd 0.556, declared one-sided 99% Student lower bound 2^-96.4282, halves -96.333 / -96.292, every diagnostic 0 (an earlier preregistered run of 32 seeds, Appendix A.9: mean 2^-96.3251, bound 2^-96.5755, not pooled); (2) the ratio of this event (E18 = E17 not imposed) to it (proof.md Section 7.5 and Appendix A.11; preregistered before the first seed): traillab shared-carrier window, 400 fresh seeds x 2^24 samples, both events counted on the same samples, ratio 1.420 (0.5054 bit), jackknife SE 0.0387, declared one-sided 99% lower bound 0.4149 bit; q3_model = 2^-96.4282 x 2^0.4149 = 2^-96.0133. Our replica (an independent implementation, Section 7.3): 960 calibration replicates, mean 2^-96.3095, every success rebuilt into a verified 38-step semi-free-start collision and accepted by the counted program; the organizer experiment a0-q3-r38 runs it with a pass rule frozen before its calibration (pooled mean of 20 >= 2^-97.0). 1a695f0b's estimator for its event (quoted): mean 2^-96.3683 over 20 runs. No transfer between classes or events is used.
heuristics.limitations: A product of two Monte-Carlo lower bounds (confidence at least 97%: the first is the larger of the bounds of two preregistered runs) measured with our own tool, which is not shipped (65,536-byte source limit); the replica and 1a695f0b's estimator are other implementations whose means agree with it within 0.05 bit. The ratio comes from a few lineage clusters per seed; H3 and the replica do not cover the extra pairs (E18 different from E17). The replica estimates a lower bound (E18 = E17 as printed, row-19 proposals from 1a695f0b's twelve conditions, W23 in F23, the characteristic's path from row 22). The bound treats the 128 seeds as independent replicates (the seed is the cluster); the mean of per-seed log2 values is conservative for log2 q3 (Jensen).

heuristics.statement: Let R_f be the number of selected variants of first block f that are good and pass row 16, and A_t the event that trial t = (f, a0) succeeds. Averaged over successes, the other variants of the same first block pass row 16 at most 2^-7.5 times: sum_t Pr[A_t] E[R_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-7.5 E[X_f].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= E[X_f] - E[X_f (X_f - 1)]/2 >= (1 - 2^-8.5) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Under H1 the law of (CV1, a0) given a success is the law of the successes of the Step-3 sampler (proof.md Section 13.5). Our measurement on successes of the accepted event: 12,028 successes of 8 independent runs of the replica's sampler (all 8 classes, a0 uniform on the 196,608 variants), each rebuilt into a verified pair and accepted by step3b, every selected variant of every passing class of its chaining value tested: 32 other row-16 passes against 21.95 under independence, 2^-8.55 per success, one-sided 99% upper bounds 2^-7.97 (Poisson) and 2^-7.79 (Student over the 8 runs), below the premise; the stage-3a passes of the other variants are at 1.0008 of their expectation. 1a695f0b measured 2 other row-16 passes on 750 successes (quoted).
heuristics.limitations: The successes are sampled by the replica's sampler, a sub-event of the accepted event (row-19 relation sets, W23 in F23, zero differences from row 22), not real collisions; successes within a run share ancestors (the Student bound uses the 8 independent runs). The other row-16 passes exceed independence by a factor 1.46 (z = +2.15); the premise counts row-16 passes only, which is conservative. No organizer execution.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^78 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^78 is the largest allowance (0.58% of T); it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (78.09276).
heuristics.extrapolation: P8's search is published with its run log (1a695f0b Section 3.2, quoted; participant-run): 38 solver runs of at most 10,800 s (230,183 s in all), P8 found in 4,714 s with a 662-s coupling check; its author bounds the search, S, the class data and all development by one 10-core machine for less than 2^21 core-seconds, which at our measured 3,797,484 SHA-256 compressions per second is 2^43.61 units, 34.4 bits under A_C. Our own measurements of the same kind of search (proof.md Appendix C, from fb176310): a 39-step characteristic derived from scratch with the public tool of [LLW24] in 2^36.04 units; published figures up to 2^39.15 units. A_C is fb176310's value, kept for the same accounting; 1a695f0b charges 2^48.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance, not our measurement: we did not rerun P8's search; its log and the 2^21 core-second bound are the author's. With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 85.88207.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) and the 8 class descriptors with their product description are obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^74 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^74, 0.036% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: 1a695f0b obtained the pair in its 662-s coupling check and the class descriptors by 32 passes over a hash of c7 (quoted); our exhaustive pass over all 2^32 values of a0 (p8fam.c, 102 s, 69 MB peak) reproduces the 8 classes and their 24,576 members each, and selftest checks the product description. A_S is fb176310's value.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance: the pair search was run by 1a695f0b, not by us; its memory (2^28.094, measured by its author) sets the claimed peak (H6).

heuristics.statement: All development of this package (exhaustive passes, end-to-end runs, the q3 runs, the replica's development and calibration, the H3 measurement, the program scans and the cloud checks of the hoisted programs; failed trials and reruns included) is at most DEV = 2^70 target compressions. H4c is a time charge; the memory figure is H6.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^70, 0.0023% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: Recorded development below 2 x 10^5 CPU-seconds (proof.md Section 13.4); at 10^10 word operations per CPU-second that is below 2^51 operations = 2^39.6 compressions, so 2^70 is more than 2^30 times the recorded work. Every development execution that produces data the attack uses ran under a hard address-space cap of 2^27 or 2^28 bytes with its peak measured by memmeter (the shared-carrier runs of proof.md Section 7.5 by /usr/bin/time -v, at most 2^27.74 bytes), at most 2^27.77 bytes (proof.md Section 14 (c2), Appendix A.10). The q3 measurements of proof.md Section 7.4 are evidence for H2, not computations of the attack: the attack reads no data they produce, so they are neither a counted phase nor charged in DEV (Section 14 (c3)).
heuristics.limitations: Accounting of our own runs, not an organizer log; declared here because the review of fb176310 recorded it as an implicit heuristic (H-implicit-development-bound). There are no other development executions in this construction.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5, a straight-line word-RAM program that evaluates E16x = C16 + W0 + s0(W1) and its stage-3a test for 256 variants at once (bit L of every 256-bit word belongs to variant L) is charged its instruction list: every load, store and spill is counted, 64 registers, complements are free except in a mixed and/or (one more operation), no fused AND-NOT; one stage-2 program per batch, with the batch's constant bits of a0 folded into it, and one stage-1 program per (class, G1) whose stored planes the 32 stage-2 programs of its y values load (each store and each load is an instruction and is counted); no target compression is evaluated this way.
heuristics.scope: The plane-program term of the ledger (37,290.96 of the 44,250.51 data-dependent operations per first block).
heuristics.extrapolation: The 24 stage-1 and 768 stage-2 programs are generated and counted by experiments/a0hoist38.py (build_e16, group, Prog.schedule, run_prog): 574 to 579 instructions per stage-1 program and 681 to 725 per stage-2 program (mean 701.65), spills of at most 10 slots; every stage-2 program is executed with its stage-1 program by the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 on all its 256 lanes and compared with the scalar definition (196,608 lanes per request in the local emulation, 0 mismatches), as are the batches of the passing classes of its trials 0..5 and 6 sampled batches in selftest; on the cloud 23,592,960 lanes of 120 random chaining values, 0 mismatches.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited; the same reading was accepted for fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2. Program generation is charged 2^32 operations per program, not counted instruction by instruction. With a scalar evaluation (38 operations per variant) the claim would be 88.86369 (sens.py, proof.md Appendix A.7).

heuristics.statement: The peak memory is the maximum over the counted phases, <= 2^28.094 bytes (claim memory_log2_bytes = 28.094). The counted phases are the online program (17,734,944 bytes = 2^24.08: the code of the 24 stage-1 and 768 stage-2 programs at 32 bytes per instruction, the hoisted planes, the tables, planes and state), the computations behind the advice (the largest is the Step-1 solve of P8, measured by its author at 279,720 KB = 2^28.094 bytes) and the development executions (run under address-space caps of 2^27 and 2^28 bytes, measured peaks at most 2^27.77 bytes).
heuristics.scope: The memory metric of the claim and the score 85.43385 + (28.094 - 20) = 93.52785.
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 14 lists every online component; the computations behind P8 measured by 1a695f0b (Step-1 solve 2^28.094, signed search at most 2^27.92, class descriptors 2^25.14; single-threaded, sequential, quoted); our solver instances (fb176310: 2^26.82 to 2^27.56); our development executions measured with /usr/bin/time -v (largest: the trail tool at 4 threads, 2^27.48) and run under prlimit --as caps with memmeter (Section 14 (c2), Appendix A.10); the organizer experiments run within the 128 MiB sandbox (66 MB and 27 MB peaks under Linux).
heuristics.limitations: The 2^28.094 figure is the author's sampled measurement (every 0.2 s), not ours; the machine model defines no code size (32 bytes per instruction is the generous choice).

heuristics.statement: In the hoisting step, two Boolean DAG nodes of the 32 batch programs with equal 512-bit evaluation signatures compute the same function (no false equivalence), so merging them leaves the generated program equal to the unhoisted one.
heuristics.scope: The node merging of the hoisted plane program (proof.md Section 9, hoisting): whether the generated program computes the reference row-16 filter. The counted operations are those of the generated program as written, exact whatever it computes; a false merge could only change which pairs pass the filter, hence the success probability, and every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory. The generated program agrees bit for bit with the reference on 23,592,960 cloud lanes (0 disagreements) and the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 (196,608 lanes, 0 mismatches); a false merge would change outputs on a positive fraction of inputs.
heuristics.limitations: Our theory, not a theorem: equal 512-bit evaluation signatures are taken to mean equal functions. Checked on 23,592,960 cloud lanes and the organizer's 196,608 lanes with 0 disagreements, not on all inputs.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is a verified collision of the target (Lemma 6.1, proof.md Section 6.1).

Algorithm: the two-block attack of ePrint 2026/1120 with the characteristic P8 of dariolina's 1a695f0b (its cells, its semi-free-start pair and the Step-1 solution S; member x = M) and the A0-variant method of fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2: 8 classes of 24,576 variants (mask 7fe96c7c, 1a695f0b's selection); one W7 test decides a class, every variant of a passing class is a good pair; per class and G1 a stage-1 plane program computes once the planes that do not depend on the 32 high-bit values y, and 768 straight-line stage-2 batch programs (the batch's constant bits of a0 folded) load them and evaluate E16x for 256 variants and test the 8 lowest bits shared by the 160 row-16 words; passing lanes resolved in scalar form; a row-16 pass is checked through row 21 (row 19 on its signed differences only, the relation E18 = E17 not imposed); rows 22..37 are computed untested and the output words of both members compared (proof.md Section 6.1).

Cost: fixed caps. N_FB = 3,013,561,795,059,207,488,300,307 first blocks (2^81.31774), each one target compression plus 35 counted operations, and V_MAX = 133,353,671,090,742,250,245,392,336,513 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded, tested at the start of every first block and after every class; at most V_MAX + 72,644,196, proof.md Lemma 8.1); allowances A_C = 2^78, A_S = 2^74 and the development charge DEV = 2^70 (H4a, H4b, H4c); counted precomputation 2^42.607 operations; final verification. Counted program: experiments/a0hoist38.py (24 stage-1 programs of 574 to 579 instructions, 768 stage-2 programs of 681 to 725 instructions, 2,825 operations for a row-16 pass). Exact total 2^85.4338498 (proof.md Section 11, Appendix B), claimed 85.43385.

Success probability at least 0.39 (the bound is exactly 0.39) under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks), H2 (q3 >= 2^-96.0133 for the accepted event of proof.md Section 6.1: 2^-96.4282, the one-sided 99% lower bound of our preregistered 128-seed measurement of the printed-cell event over the 196,608 selected variants (mean 2^-96.3123), times the preregistered lower bound 0.4149 bit of the ratio of this event to it, proof.md Section 7.5) and H3 (averaged over successes, the other variants of the same first block pass row 16 at most 2^-7.5 times; measured 2^-8.55), by Bonferroni per first block, independence across first blocks and Chebyshev for the work cap; a cap halt happens only if the total work exceeds V_MAX, probability at most P_cap 1.015e-30, inside the bound (proof.md Section 10). No expected-work bound is used.

Memory: peak 2^28.094 bytes = maximum over the counted phases: online 17,734,944 bytes; preprocessing: the Step-1 solve of P8 measured by its author at 279,720 KB = 2^28.094 bytes; the development executions, run under address-space caps of at most 2^28 bytes (peaks at most 2^27.77); the q3 measurements are evidence for H2, not phases of the attack. H6. Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 85.43385 + 8.094 = 93.52785. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.
